status: MEASURED on the corrected instrument (task-8, plan 2.53); supersedes the retracted plan 2.46

design.xi: weight_i * s_i with the leave-one-out baseline; s_i from the corrected readout
design.estimators: pooled ANOVA (one pool of 256, global baseline) vs split-half curve r(K)=K/(K+2κ) (disjoint halves, per context)

old_vs_new.claim: old "1500 vs 1424 agree within 5%" is dead on two counts: it compared κ with 2κ, and it compared two different estimators

verdict: the noise-to-signal ratio is 217.6 by the split-half-consistent route (from the measured r(32)=0.0685 of plan 2.51), and that value lies INSIDE the context-bootstrap interval. The pooled ANOVA point estimate is 6403.7, ~29x larger, and it is the estimator the audit showed to be invalid (E[f(X)] != f(E[X]); a global baseline mixed with between-context variation). So the defensible number is kappa ~ 217 (interval from the bootstrap), i.e. ~217 rollouts per context for r=0.5 - not 1500, and certainly not the ambient dimension. No claim of independent agreement is made: the two routes are compared only through the interval.
per_context_dominance: the per-context sum||xi||^2 spans 6.4e+07..2.7e+09, so the pooled trace is dominated by a few contexts - which is exactly why the pooled point estimate is not trustworthy
